title: Claude's note: tech sell-off, inflation and a strategy change
lead: What moved the market and our stocks on October 12–15. The automatic daily brief above refreshes itself; this note was written by hand and is shown only on the day it was written and the day after.

items.head: Inflation and the Fed
items.text: September consumer prices rose 3.7% from a year earlier (forecast 3.6%, August 3.4%); core inflation rose to 2.6%. Energy drove more than half of the increase. New York Fed President John Williams said one more rate hike this year would be appropriate, and the 10-year Treasury yield climbed to 5.27%. Higher rates hit technology stocks hardest, because their prices rest on profits expected far in the future.

items.head: AI and chip sell-off
items.text: The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell about 10% in six sessions, erasing close to $1 trillion in value; South Korea's stock market fell about 12% in five days. Investors are questioning when the huge AI investments will pay off. This is why our 3x semiconductor fund (SOXL) hit its stop-loss.

items.head: Dell
items.text: Barclays cut Dell, HPE and NetApp from buy to hold: it sees no clear pickup in corporate AI spending and thinks the stocks ran up too far. Dell fell 8–11% that day and Super Micro about 7%. Dell still has a $95 billion AI order backlog, so demand exists; the question is timing. The old bot sold Dell twice at a loss during this drop.

items.head: Snowflake
items.text: No single piece of news: a rich valuation (about 169 times expected earnings), competition from Amazon and Microsoft and continued losses met the tech sell-off, and the stock fell 4–6% on October 14. Product revenue had grown 37% last quarter.

items.head: TSMC (today)
items.text: The world's largest chipmaker reported third-quarter revenue of $46.7 billion (+50.9%) and a 66.4% gross margin, and guided $52.3–54.3 billion for the fourth quarter. AI demand is real; the sell-off is mostly about interest rates and valuations.

items.head: Oil and geopolitics
items.text: Brent crude is above $105 a barrel as Houthi attacks on Saudi energy facilities continue. Expensive energy pushes inflation up, and inflation pushes rate expectations up.

items.head: Banks
items.text: Bank of America's third-quarter profit fell 17% because of a $1.2 billion regulatory penalty and weaker trading revenue; BlackRock and Morgan Stanley beat expectations. Money moved from technology into the more traditional companies of the Dow.

items.head: What it meant for us
items.text: All of the old bot's long positions were in AI and software stocks and were carried with 2.3x leverage, so the sector sell-off hit them all at once, and tight stop-losses sold near the bottom. The backtest showed that this strategy also lost money over the long run. The bot switched today to the unleveraged v4: half QQQ, half a monthly momentum basket spread across sectors, and cash whenever the market trend breaks.
